items.summary: his work studies the basin geometry of the negative integer Collatz map. Under exact iteration of T(n)={n/2,n even,3n+1,n odd,T(n)= \begin{cases} n/2, & n \text{ even},\\ 3n+1, & n \text{ odd}, \end{cases} the first 10710^7 negative integers are observed to enter one of the three classical negative cycles through −1-1 , −5-5 , and −17-17 . The corresponding empirical basin proportions stabilize near 0.327:0.324:0.3480.327:0.324:0.348 , with a persistent modest excess for the C−17C_{-17} basin. The paper then examines the structure behind these basin frequencies. Basin membership is found to be weakly predicted by simple residue classes modulo 2k2^k , and short prefixes of the 22 -adic valuation itinerary under the accelerated odd Collatz map show essentially no transferable predictive power in held-out tests. A markedly different structure appears in the reverse dynamics. Monotone inverse trees rooted in the three negative attractors show strongly unequal relative sizes, stabilizing near 0.293:0.218:0.4890.293:0.218:0.489 . The associated tree-count ratios remain highly stable over repeated increases in the magnitude cutoff, motivating a common reverse-growth conjecture with basin-dependent amplitudes. Forward trajectories partially erase this reverse-tree asymmetry. Low-reversal trajectories are strongly enriched for the C−17C_{-17} attractor, while increasing non-monotone trajectory complexity attenuates that advantage and moves the observed basin shares closer to the near-balanced global census. The resulting empirical picture is that asymmetric reverse accessibility and forward trajectory mixing jointly shape the macroscopic basin distribution. The paper proposes corresponding conjectures on negative basin densities and reverse-tree ratio convergence. These computations do not prove that every negative integer enters one of the three known cycles, do not exclude additional negative cycles or divergent orbits, and do not resolve the positive Collatz conjecture. The contribution is a computational study of basin structure, reverse accessibility, and mixing in the signed integer extension of the Collatz map.
items.title: Negative-Basin Geometry in the Integer Collatz Map: Forward Census, Reverse-Tree Asymmetry, and Mixing

items.summary: We study explicit algebraic cycles and the recovery of their supports in three special fourfold settings. For a smooth diagonal intersection of five quadrics in P⁹, a paired splitting plane in the associated ten-hyperplane arrangement produces an orbit of thirty-two degree-four del Pezzo surfaces. Their alternating rational cycle w has square 3. An elliptic-quartic net gives an actual correspondence D = w × η to P² and the Chow projector w × w/3. The paired incidence is smooth of dimension twelve, finite and locally immersed over the sixteen-dimensional diagonal moduli space, and has a nonempty non-evaluation open. Its tangent quotient is an Artinian reduction of the Segre ring of P² × P², with Hilbert function (1, 4, 1). We use this quotient and the relative cycles to identify the complete marked Hodge germ with the paired incidence branch, including its scheme structure. At a very general paired point, the full-character rational Hodge sector is exactly ℚw; the proper characters give the rational Hodge conjecture for these very general fourfolds. The germ statement concerns diagonal deformations. For hypersurface fourfolds of degree d ≥ 5, we prove a reverse recognition theorem. A tangent-exhausting integrated Hodge family with a persistent embedded connected-sum annihilator forces its two candidate ambient planes to lie on the hypersurface and recovers the full rationally weighted primitive class. The conormal variation is surjective onto the true graded ideal-deformation space and has a seventeen-dimensional kernel. An explicit smooth family shows that the equation can nevertheless fail to belong to the square of its Hodge annihilator. Finally, from Paranjape's K3–Prym correspondence we construct a quadratic trace and an explicit sheared odd correspondence, purify it by rational endomorphism selectors, and compute its full and primitive kernels under a stated full Hodge-group hypothesis. Weil-class algebraicity is already known; this part concerns an explicit realization and its action. Further constructions record exact Chow returns and several rigidity phenomena. All genericity restrictions and the distinction between Chow identities, complex Hodge dimensions, and rational Hodge spaces are retained.
items.title: Explicit Hodge Classes and Support Recognition on Special Fourfolds

items.summary: This dataset provides raw LC-MS data files (instrument .raw format) from an untargeted lipidomics analysis of mouse liver, intended as a demonstration dataset for LipiRich (website: https://lipirich.sarahehancock.com , github: https://github.com/sarahehancock/LipiRich ), an open-source Shiny application for normalisation, statistical analysis, and visualisation of untargeted lipidomics data exported from MS-DIAL 5. Sample origin: Liver tissue was obtained from C57BL/6J mice from three dietary groups (n = 8 per group): standard chow, lard-based high-fat diet (45% of energy from fat; 88% lard, 12% safflower oil), and a high-fat diet in which 90% of the lard was substituted with fish oil. Animals and diets are as described in Liu et al. (2014), Scientific Reports 4:5538 ( https://doi.org/10.1038/srep05538 ), from which these liver samples were retained. Lipid extraction: Lipids were extracted from liver tissue (~20 mg) using a modified methyl-tert-butyl ether (MTBE) method. Tissue was homogenized in ice-cold 150 mM ammonium acetate (10 mg tissue/100 μL) using a bead homogenizer, kept below 4°C. Aliquots of homogenate (1 mg equivalent) were added to MTBE:methanol (3:1 v/v, 0.01% BHT) together with a mixed internal standard solution (100 pmol each of PC 17:0/17:0, PE 17:0/17:0, PS 17:0/17:0, PG 17:0/17:0, PA 17:0/17:0 LPC 17:0, LPE 14:0, ceramide d18:1/17:0, dihydrosphingomyelin d18:0/12:0, DAG 15:0/15:0, d-TAG 48:0, and CE 22:1; 10 pmol each d3-palmitoyl carnitine, lactosylceramide 12:0 and glucosylceramide 15:0; 1 nmol cholesterol-d7, 50 pmol PI 15:0_18:1-d7, and 5 pmol N-acylethanolamine 17:1). Samples were rotated at 4°C overnight, then one volume of ice-cold 150 mM ammonium acetate was added, vortexed, and centrifuged to separate phases. The upper organic phase was dried under nitrogen at 37°C and reconstituted in 200 μL chloroform:methanol:water (60:30:4.5 v/v/v; 200 μL) prior to analysis. LC-MS acquisition: Lipids were separated on a C18 reverse-phase column (Waters Acquity CSH, 2.1 × 100 mm, 1.7 µm) using a binary gradient (mobile phase A: acetonitrile:water 6:4 v/v; mobile phase B: isopropanol:acetonitrile 9:1 v/v; both containing 10 mM ammonium formate and 0.1% formic acid), at 0.26 mL/min with the column oven at 60°C. The gradient was as follows: 0−1.5 min isocratic elution with 32% B; from 1.5 to 4 min increase to 45% B, from 4 to 5 min increase to 52% B, from 5 to 8 min to 58% B, from 8 to 11 min to 66% B, from 11 to 14 min to 70% B, from 14 to 18 min to 75% B, from 18 to 21 min to 97% B, during 21 to 25 min 97% B is maintained; from 25−25.1 min solvent B was decreased to 32% and then maintained for another 4.9 min for column re-equilibration (Hu et al. 2008 J Proteome Res , 7(11), https://doi.org/10.1021/pr800373m ). Data were acquired on a Q Exactive HF mass spectrometer (ThermoFisher) with a heated electrospray ionization source, in both positive (spray voltage 4.0 kV) and negative (3.5 kV) ion mode, using full-scan/data-dependent MS2 acquisition (full-scan resolution 70,000 FWHM, scan range m/z 200–1,500, top 10 data-dependent ions per cycle, normalized stepped collision energy 15/27 eV, MS2 resolution 17,500). Mass calibration was performed in both ionization modes prior to analysis. Processing note: These are the original instrument .raw files prior to any peak picking, alignment, or annotation. They are intended to be processed through MS-DIAL 5 by the end user (recommended starting parameters: minimum peak height 1×10⁴ cps, MS1 tolerance 0.01 Da, MS2 tolerance 0.025 Da, minimum identification score 50%, retention time alignment tolerance 0.5 min), and are provided so that users of LipiRich can practise the full workflow starting from raw instrument output, or reprocess with their own MS-DIAL parameters. MS-DIAL parameter files and ISTD as msp libraries are provided on GitHub File contents: chow_13_pos, chow_6_pos, chow_4_pos, chow_7_pos, chow_5_pos, c
items.title: Untargeted LC-MS lipidomics of mouse liver from chow, lard, and fish oil-fed C57BL/6 mice: demonstration dataset for LipiRich

items.summary: A provenance analysis for a query evaluation or a model checking computation extracts information on how its result depends on the atomic facts of the model or database. Traditional work on data provenance was, to a large extent, restricted to positive query languages or the negation-free fragment of first-order logic and showed how provenance abstractions can be usefully described as elements of commutative semirings -- most generally as multivariate polynomials with positive integer coefficients. We describe and evaluate here a provenance approach for dealing with negation, based on quotient semirings of polynomials with dual indeterminates. This not only provides a semiring provenance analysis for full first-order logic (and other logics and query languages with negation) but also permits a reverse provenance analysis, i.e., finding models that satisfy various properties under given provenance tracking assumptions. We describe the potential for applications to explaining missing query answers or failures of integrity constraints, and to using these explanations for computing repairs. This approach also is the basis of a systematic study of semiring semantics in a broad logical context.
items.title: Provenance Analysis and Semiring Semantics for First-Order Logic

items.summary: European digital sovereignty and security increasingly depend on whether high-impact decisions can be grounded in location evidence that remains credible under adversarial pressure. This paper frames a cross-sector analysis as a location-data provenance problem: whether there is contestable evidence about where and when an asserted event occurred, who or what produced the assertion, what a device or service reported as location, and which audit and retention guarantees apply. Trust-erosion patterns are observable across democratic processes and the information environment, trade and origin-sensitive supply chains, finance and illicit shipping flows, critical infrastructure and mobility, and harms targeting individuals' private and social domains. In these patterns we see a recurring asymmetry in which locality, presence, routing, or jurisdiction can be asserted cheaply while institutions and affected parties face costly reconstruction when disputes arise. To make this challenge actionable, this paper introduces a compact risk taxonomy that decomposes provenance failures into integrity axes and recurring failure modes, and derives design expectations for next-generation digital trust infrastructure centered on contestability under dispute, while remaining privacy- and rights-compatible. It argues for treating location as a digital primitive that should be represented as evidence-bearing claims rather than self-asserted coordinates, and positions proof-of-location (PoL) mechanisms as a candidate capability layer for producing verifiable presence claims under explicit threat and privacy assumptions. The outcome is a sector-neutral foundation for future architectural work on a next-generation digital trust infrastructure for Europe.
items.title: Where Trust Fails: Mapping Location-Data Provenance Risks in Europe

items.summary: This reproducibility package accompanies a measurement-science workflow for temporal light modulation (TLM) metric reproduction and computational sensitivity analysis. Five independent MK350S Premium optical waveform records form the bounded commercial demonstration. MetTLM W1–W20 public references support source-traceable PstLM/SVM calculation-pipeline reproduction and sampling-rate, duration and deterministic modelled-effect sensitivity analyses. Evidence identity is preserved so that public waveforms, resampled/windowed/perturbed rows and auxiliary electrical/photometric records are not treated as additional commercial observations. The package includes the five commercial raw waveform files, machine-readable commercial/context summaries, source code, public-reference provenance and checksums, frozen MetTLM reproduction outputs, sampling/duration/modelled-effect outputs, journal-neutral numerical and claim-boundary QC files and a journal-neutral manuscript snapshot. Raw third-party public-reference assets and manufacturer documents are intentionally not redistributed; original DOI/license/checksum provenance and reconstruction scripts are provided instead. The package supports calculation-pipeline reproduction and bounded commercial SVM-related screening. It does not constitute IEC certification, physical calibration, commercial-lamp PstLM, measurement uncertainty, commercial repeatability, PF–SVM causality or population-level generalization.
items.title: Reproducibility Package for Public-Reference Reproduction and Sensitivity Analysis of Temporal Light Modulation Metrics Using MetTLM

items.summary: Parametric models of the human head are essential tools traditionally used in computer vision and graphics for animation, rendering, and reconstruction. More recently, they serve as crucial conditioning signals within generative large vision models, allowing for tight spatial control of generated imagery. However, existing publicly available models are typically limited in anatomical scope, modeling only outer geometry while ignoring intra-oral and ocular structures, and frequently suffer from reduced geometric quality stemming from low-fidelity input datasets. In this report we introduce a new parametric model dubbed Generative aNthropometric Model (GNM), named as a homophone of the human genome. GNM encompasses the head, face, neck, eyeballs, teeth, and tongue, and it is built on an extensive database of high-resolution 3D scans combined with high-quality anatomy specific artist-made samples. This report details the data provenance, the model architecture including the specialized sub-models for the ocular and intra-oral structures, and shows its SotA performance on fitting target 3D face scans. To foster community innovation, the complete GNM framework is made publicly available.
items.title: GNM Head: A Generative aNthropometric Model of the human head

items.summary: This record contains the preprint paper "LOST IN THE PDFS: CONTEXT DEGRADATION AND PARAMETRIC HALLUCINATIONS IN LLM UIS" , authored by Gabriele D’Iorio (University of Naples Parthenope).  The study investigates the structural limitations and operational vulnerabilities of commercial web-based Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces when handling long, multi-document sequential workflows in educational contexts. Abstract: The growing use of LLMs for educational purposes, especially by inexperienced users, inevitably leads to LLMs hallucinating and making mistakes. This study presents an experiment using the web version of Gemini (Pro Standard and Flash Standard modes) to simulate a numerical analysis class covering three topics (interpolation, piecewise interpolation, and approximation), each in a separate PDF. This study is subdivided into two scenarios created to evaluate how the LLM responded and, above all, to see how long it took to hallucinate or suffer from context degradation. The results demonstrate the failure of both scenarios due to context degradation. Despite large theoretical context windows, sudden attachment truncation in the web UI forces the model to rely on its parametric memory, leading to severe hallucinations and sycophantic behavior. Key Topics Covered: - Context Degradation & "Lost in the Middle" Phenomenon: Analysis of how LLMs lose retrieval accuracy in prolonged sessions. - Parametric Hallucinations: How models compensate for context loss by fabricating details from pre-training data. - Document Parsing Challenges: Visual layout issues in standard Web UIs. - Experimental Evaluation: A comparative analysis of a single-chat setup (Scenario A) versus a dual-agent/tutor setup (Scenario B). Data Availability: The comprehensive dataset, interaction logs, prompt configurations, and Python scripts used for token counting are openly accessible in the project’s GitHub repository at: https://github.com/gabpolymath/lost_in_the_pdfs/
items.title: Lost in the PDFs: Context Degradation and Parametric Hallucinations in LLM UIs

items.summary: Generative AI is reshaping how research software is developed. Tools and patterns ranging from “vibe coding” through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and autonomous agents now offer compelling productivity gains, but their adoption in scientific computing surfaces failure modes that general-purpose evaluation does not catch: silent unit conversions, violated conservation laws, hallucinated physics, loss of numerical precision, and quietly broken reproducibility. These failures share a signature: nothing visible goes wrong. The AI ecosystem itself is moving fast, leaving RSEs to make consequential integration decisions with little shared vocabulary or principled guidance. This talk introduces Scientific Agentic Engineering , the central contribution of an in-progress 2026 Better Scientific Software (BSSw) Fellowship: a tool-agnostic methodology for integrating AI agents into high-stakes scientific software workflows. The framework defines how agents, scientific skills, and MCP servers should be structured around validation loops, explicit human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and domain-specific safeguards. Every task moves through a short workflow (frame, plan and critique, implement, verify), with decisions recorded throughout, and the framework maps each documented failure mode to the stage where it is cheapest to catch. The intent is not to recommend any particular AI tool but to articulate foundational concepts that remain valid as the underlying technology changes. I will share three artifacts from the fellowship: The Framework (published July 2026). Shared vocabulary, its principles and workflow, structural guidance on where safeguards live, and a pattern catalog of named practices, each tied to the failure it counters. The Reference Workflow. A structured exercise in which RSEs use AI tools to build a small weather-model error-statistics application, applying the framework to avoid the failure modes it documents. The Community Repository. A curated starter set of scientific MCP server templates, agent skills such as unit checkers and conservation-law validators, and agent configuration examples, designed to be starting points for the community to adapt to a variety of scientific domains. These artifacts are by design community resources, and broader adoption is the explicit aim of the remaining milestones, which include an interactive online tutorial series comparing purpose-built scientific agents with general-purpose tools, a recorded live workshop published for asynchronous access, and a BSSw.io blog post directing the community to the project’s resources. This work engages the conference theme directly by advancing AI-assisted scientific software development from ad-hoc experimentation toward a disciplined, transferable engineering practice.
items.title: Scientific Agentic Engineering: A Framework for Reliable AI Agents in Research Software

items.summary: 2.2.0 A minor version, not a patch: the change below alters what a default run leaves on disk. Nothing about your results, final outputs or logs changes, but a default that deletes files users previously got to keep is more than a patch. Changed Intermediate pfiles are now deleted as the run progresses, at defaults. Each QC step reads a genotype file and writes a new one — callrate reads your input and writes …_callrate , sex reads that and writes …_sex , and so on — so a ten-step run creates ten copies of your data. At GP2 release scale each copy is tens of GiB. Cleanup used to be skipped whenever warn_only was set, and warn-and-continue is the default , so at defaults every copy survived for the whole run. The only way to reclaim the disk was --no-warn , which also turns warn-and-continue into fail-fast — so you could not have both. That is a bad trade on a long run, where warn-and-continue exists precisely so an eight-hour job does not die on one recoverable step. The two flags no longer interfere: | | before | now | |---|---|---| | (default) | keeps every copy | deletes each copy once the next is written | | --full-output | keeps every copy | keeps every copy | | --no-warn | deletes + fail-fast | fail-fast only | | --no-warn --full-output | keeps + fail-fast | keeps + fail-fast | --full-output is now the only switch governing retention; --no-warn is purely failure policy. Peak disk during a run drops from roughly one working copy per step to one overall — on the round-19 full-GP2 run, ~98 GiB written against a ~50 GiB peak. If you relied on the old default to inspect intermediates, pass --full-output — it reproduces the previous behavior exactly. A failed step's input is still kept either way, so a broken run can still be examined.
items.title: GenoTools

items.summary: The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua’s altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel’s unfinished offering, Cain’s failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is also tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses; the original connection-density test was performed on a pre-set group of 124 verses selected by the narrative. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place , the observed network produced Z = 19.37 (p < 0.0002) against 5,000 random permutations. A second, deliberately simpler test removes the seven control letters א, מ, ת, נ, י, ה, ו from every word and performs direct string matching with no root database; it still yields Z = 10.29 (p < 0.0002) , with the same major long-range connections rising to the top. A raw-word test remains significant at Z = 5.17 (p = 0.0013) . A separate anthology comparison tests whether similarly chosen biblical themes automatically generate the same effect. The Ebal/Shechem axis reaches Z = 17.35 , compared with Covenant Z = 10.07 , Jerusalem/Temple Z = 1.60 , Joseph Z = −8.13 , and Tabernacle Z = −7.16 . The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual. A scientific appendix further examines comparative anatomical and genomic parallels associated with one of the essay’s most unexpected motifs, while explicitly distinguishing scientific observation from midrashic interpretation. After fifteen years of work, the author does not regard this as a story invented to fit the text, but as part of a larger architecture that the text itself gradually disclosed — a structure he considers himself fortunate to have uncovered, even if only in part, and to place on record now. Bilingual publication: Hebrew original and English edition.
items.title: The Earth That Listened — The Hidden Timeline from Genesis to Joshua

items.summary: This record contains the publication-facing verification materials and reproducible Lean 4 certificate packages for the continuing formal validation of the Chronos Navier-Stokes program, extending the original unified clock milestone through certificate versions v1.2–v1.10. The formal development is compiled against OpenAI's public NavierStokesAndEuler repository at the pinned upstream commit using Lean 4.34.0-rc2. It begins from OpenAI's actual selected periodic Navier-Stokes candidate and extends the previously verified Chronos change, arrow, action, and aim clock into a broader temporal-field framework. The formally verified development now includes the closed temporal-exchange balance, the Chronos selector value, an exact selector-defined temporal carrier satisfying, temporal diffusion and relaxation dynamics, a nonnegative temporal-field arrow under the stated sign conditions, an independent change-arrow-aim clock for the temporal carrier, and complete oriented temporal histories including the initial endpoint. The later certificates introduce a general temporal source-law interface and formally analyze a nonlinear radial saturation source law of the form The verified results include its exact energy/action decomposition, nonlinear saturation contribution, nonnegative net arrow under the stated parameter conditions, closed instantaneous and historical clock identities, and an exact necessary-and-sufficient calibration criterion. The calibration theorem separates source identification into zero-state compatibility, directional alignment, and scalar magnitude. The formal development also proves a parameter-free transverse alignment condition and establishes that the radial law depends on the difference between drive and damping rather than identifying those two parameters independently. Taken together, versions v1.2–v1.10 extend the Chronos formal program from a verified Navier-Stokes clock decomposition into a formally connected temporal exchange, selector, carrier, field-dynamics, source-law, and calibration architecture. The uploaded certificate archives contain Lean source modules, reproduction scripts, SHA-256 checksums, build logs, provenance information, and dedicated axiom-audit results. items.summary: This repository contains two LC–MS/MS raw data files (and .mgf versions if needed), associated search parameters, and curated FASTA databases generated from purified fibrinogen clots crosslinked by endogenous FXIIIa or recombinant transglutaminase 2 (TG2). These samples represent a controlled benchmark system for evaluating crosslink-mass spectrometry (XL-MS) software performance on non-cleavable enzymatic Q–K isopeptide bonds. Unlike conventional chemical crosslinkers, these transglutaminase-mediated crosslinks are zero-length modifications formed by ammonia (NH₃) loss, creating unique challenges for false discovery control and site assignment. The datasets are provided to enable transparent, community-driven comparison of XL search engines and to advance methodological development in enzymatic crosslink identification.
items.title: Open Benchmark Dataset for Enzymatic Q–K Crosslink Identification by LC–MS/MS

items.summary: Background: Surface roughness is an important characteristic of resin composite restorations and may be influenced by material composition and finishing and polishing procedures. Objective: To evaluate changes in surface roughness (Ra) of nanofilled, nanohybrid, and microhybrid resin composites after sequential finishing and polishing and to compare their final surface roughness. Materials and Methods: S ixty disc-shaped specimens (8 mm × 2 mm; shade A2) were fabricated using Filtek Z350 XT, IPS Empress Direct, and Filtek Z250 (n = 20 per material). Fifteen specimens per material underwent a standardized finishing and polishing protocol using fine- and extra-fine-grit diamond burs followed by sequential Sof-Lex discs, while five specimens per material remained untreated as controls. Surface roughness was measured using a Mitutoyo SJ-210 contact profilometer at baseline   and after the intervention. Because specimen-level identification was not preserved between measurement sessions, baseline and final measurements were analyzed as independent observations using independent-samples t-tests, with Welch’s correction when required. Final Ra values among materials were compared using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey HSD tests (α = 0.05). Results: All three experimental composites showed statistically significant increases in Ra after finishing and polishing (all p < 0.001), whereas no statistically significant changes were observed in the untreated controls (all p > 0.05). Mean Ra increased from 0.085 to 0.181 μm for IPS Empress Direct, from 0.111 to 0.186 μm for Filtek Z350 XT, and from 0.122 to 0.195 μm for Filtek Z250. Final Ra values did not differ significantly among the three materials (F(2,42) = 0.559, p = 0.576). Conclusions: Sequential finishing and polishing significantly increased surface roughness relative to the strip-polymerized baseline surfaces of all three resin composites, without statistically significant differences in final Ra among the materials. The final mean Ra values remained below the predefined 0.2 μm surface-roughness threshold. Under the experimental conditions evaluated, post-polishing surface roughness could not be predicted solely on the basis of nanofilled, nanohybrid, or microhybrid filler classification.
items.title: Surface Roughness of Nanofilled, Nanohybrid, and Microhy-brid Resin Composites After Sequential Finishing and Polish-ing: An In Vitro Comparative Study

items.summary: A 0.1° monthly and daily terrestrial water storage anomaly (TWSA) product for the Ganga (Ganges) River Basin, 2000–2025 , together with the source code, the inputs, and the full evaluation record that produced it. GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL RL06 mascons are spatially downscaled by fitting a predictor–TWSA relation across mascons; every mascon's area-weighted aggregate is then forced back onto the observed value. The monthly field is disaggregated to daily under an exact monthly constraint, its within-month shape supplied by the ERA5-Land water balance with nothing fitted at the daily scale. Per-pixel uncertainty is reported as four separate terms rather than one number, because only some of them are measurable against an observation. What changed in v1.0.1, and what did not. The data are unchanged. The three product netCDFs, the monthly and daily COGs, the trend field and every input and intermediate archive are the same files already in this record — if you have them, there is nothing to download again, and any analysis built on v1.0.0 stands. Four files change, all of them code or documentation: grace-grb-1.0.1.zip , the source at the new tag, which adds main/trend_regions.py and the scripts behind three manuscript figures; evaluation_tables.zip , which gains trend_by_region.csv ; figures.zip , which gains those three plates; and DATA_README.md . The version exists for reproducibility rather than revision: the regional trend figures quoted in the paper were computed from a region definition that had never been committed, so a reader holding the archived trend field could not reproduce them. That definition is now in the archive, it is checked to partition the basin, and the paper cites this version. What is imposed and what is learned. Each mascon's level and linear trend are taken from GRACE rather than learned from the predictors — the secular signal here is groundwater abstraction, and no reanalysis simulates pumping. Only the sub-mascon anomaly is modelled, from 78 predictor features built on ERA5-Land and nine covariates, seven of them static and two annual cropland fractions held constant after 2022. Mass conservation then forces every mascon mean back onto the observation by a minimum-norm correction. Agreement with GRACE at mascon scale is therefore arithmetic, not evidence of skill : the basin mean of this product reproduces the GRACE basin mean at r = 1.00000, RMSE 0.27 mm. We state that plainly so it is not mistaken for validation. Held-out performance. Skill is reported only where it can be measured — at spatial units the model never saw, at times it never saw, and against an independent observation. Spatial (leave-one-mascon-out, 19 folds with a neighbour buffer): RMSE 88.2 mm, R² 0.638, NSE 0.635 over 83,309 held-out cell-months. Cluster bootstrap over mascons (2,000 resamples): RMSE 82.1–95.1 mm, R² 0.580–0.694. Temporal (whole months held out): interior gap-filling RMSE 71.7 mm (R² 0.775); scattered months 74.5 mm (0.713), a random split and so optimistic — each withheld month keeps its neighbours in training; out-of-record extrapolation 91.1 mm (0.730) . The last is the regime the post-2024 months live in. Independent (656 quality-controlled CGWB dug wells): at basin scale the downscaled field reaches r = 0.814, RMSE 57.0 mm against a bilinear-interpolation baseline at r = 0.742, RMSE 73.1 mm. Skill is strongly scale-dependent: median R² is 0.48 per mascon but 0.19 per well, and NSE exceeds zero at only 168 of 656 wells. Neither side is ground truth — a well is a point head times an estimated specific yield, the product a 0.1° cell from a 3° mascon — so the scale dependence is reported as the result rather than a single pooled number. items.summary: Electric vehicles (EVs) experience significant  driving  range degradation in low ambient temperature conditions, primarily due to the elevated energy demand of heating system.  T his paper proposes  an optimal  control strategy for a  positive temperature coefficient ( PTC )  heater-based electric minibus  heating system ,  which is  aimed to  exploit actuators’ redundancy for  energy consumption  minimization  and driving range extension . The strategy  optimally  allocates  control inputs  of multiple actuators  to  provide  heating power demand ed  by a superimposed proportional-integral (PI)  feedback  controller of the  passenger  cabin air temperatur e .  The  optimal  allocation maps prescri be  coolant pump flow, blower air   flow, and inlet air temperature references , and they  are obtained by comprehensive simulations of a high-fidelity multi-physics heating system model over a wide range of quasi-stationary operating conditions .   A low-level PI controller is further designed for the full ,  allocation-related range of operating points to track the  allocated  inlet air temperature reference, while commanding the PTC heater power.   The overall control strategy is validated through co-simulation with a high-fidelity vehicle model  in comparison with an industry baseline strategy , demonstrating a considerable energy consumption reduction in both quasi-stationary and transient (heat up) conditions, as well as improved control performance in terms of shorter heat up intervals.
items.title: Optimal Control Allocation Strategy for an Energy-efficient PTC Heater-based Electric Vehicle Passenger Cabin Heating System

items.summary: Abstract Background  Thyroid dysfunction is one of the most common endocrine disorders affecting metabolic activity, psychological well-being, and gastrointestinal function.(1,2) Patients frequently experience elevated thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) levels, stress, bloating, impaired digestion, reduced metabolic efficiency, and decreased quality of life. Although conventional treatment effectively restores thyroid hormone balance in many patients, complementary therapeutic interventions are increasingly being explored to improve overall clinical outcomes and patient-reported health status.  Aim  To evaluate the effect of a Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid on thyroid function, perceived stress, gastrointestinal symptoms, and participant-reported global improvement among adults with thyroid dysfunction.  Materials and Methods:  A prospective, single-arm interventional clinical study was conducted involving  22 adult participants  diagnosed with thyroid dysfunction. Baseline demographic characteristics including age, body weight, height, and body mass index (BMI) were recorded. Clinical assessments included serum thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH), perceived stress score (0–40 scale), gastrointestinal symptoms related to bloating, digestion, and metabolism, and Participant Global Impression of Change (PGIC). All parameters were assessed before and after the intervention. The composition of the study formulation will be described separately. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate descriptive and inferential statistical methods, and statistical significance was considered at  p  < 0.05.  Results:  The intervention demonstrated an overall improvement in multiple clinical outcomes. Mean serum TSH decreased from  10.27 to 3.77 mIU/L , while mean perceived stress scores decreased from  20.45 to 13.18 . Improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms and PGIC scores was observed in the majority of participants. Perceived stress scores decreased in a substantial proportion of participants, indicating improvement in psychological well-being. Gastrointestinal symptoms such as bloating and impaired digestion improved from mild or moderate severity to normal or minimal symptoms in the majority of cases. Participant-reported outcomes also demonstrated favorable changes, with PGIC scores increasing in most participants, suggesting meaningful overall clinical improvement. The intervention was generally well tolerated, and no serious adverse events were documented during the study period.  Conclusion:  The findings of this prospective clinical study suggest that the investigated Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid may contribute to improved thyroid function, reduction in perceived stress, better gastrointestinal health, and enhanced patient-reported quality of life in adults with thyroid dysfunction. These preliminary findings support the potential role of the formulation as a complementary therapeutic option. Larger randomized controlled clinical trials with extended follow-up are warranted to confirm these observations and establish long-term efficacy and safety.   Keywords: Thyroid Dysfunction; Thyroid Stimulating Hormone; TSH; Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid; Teacurry Thyroid Tea; Teacurry; Thyroid Tea; Herbal Tea for Thyroid; Complementary ##plugin
items.title: Effect of a Plant-Based Herbal Tea Formulation "Teacurry Thyro Herb Tea for Thyroid" on Thyroid Function, TSH Levels, Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Participant-Reported Global Improvement in Adults with Thyroid Dysfunction: Real-World Evidence Clinical Study

items.summary: AUST_2026_BAT is a global bathymetric model developed using multi-scale marine gravity anomaly features, fully connected deep neural networks (FCDNNs), and an adaptive multi-factor spatial partitioning (AMFSP) framework. The dataset covers 180°W–180°E and 75°S–75°N at a spatial resolution of 1′ × 1′. The oceanic portion represents the modeled bathymetry, while land elevations are filled using the land component of GEBCO_2025, forming a spatially continuous topographic–bathymetric grid over the entire model domain. AUST_2026_BAT was generated using SIO V33.1 marine gravity anomalies and quality-controlled shipborne bathymetric observations from the National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI). The marine gravity field was decomposed into multi-scale features, including long-wavelength gravity anomalies (LG), short-wavelength gravity anomalies (SG), and their corresponding residual components (RLG and RSG), to represent gravity–bathymetry relationships at different spatial scales and retain complementary residual information for bathymetric prediction. To account for regional variations in seafloor morphology, gravity–bathymetry relationships, observational coverage, and coastal conditions, the global domain was divided into 60 primary 30° × 30° regions and further partitioned using the AMFSP framework based on water depth, seafloor slope, gravity anomaly, shipborne sounding density, and distance from the coastline. FCDNN models were then trained for individual subregions, and predictions in overlapping areas were merged using a standard-deviation-weighted blending strategy to generate the final continuous global bathymetric surface. Independent validation using shipborne bathymetric observations shows good overall agreement between AUST_2026_BAT and measured seafloor depths. Comparisons with existing global bathymetric models, including GEBCO_2025, SIO topo_27.1, and SRTM15+ V2.7, indicate lower overall prediction errors for AUST_2026_BAT, with the improvements being more pronounced in deep-water regions and generally consistent performance across the major ocean basins.
items.title: AUST_2026_BAT: A Global Bathymetry Model Derived from Multi-Scale Marine Gravity Anomalies Using Fully Connected Deep Neural Networks and Adaptive Multi-Factor Spatial Partitioning

items.summary: Per-pixel  active-flame  image–mask chips from  Sentinel-2  covering  25 large California wildfires  (acquisitions spanning 2020–2026). The deposit contains  2,148  co-registered pairs of false-colour composites and segmentation masks. Each chip is  512 × 512 pixels at 20 m  (~10.24 km across), rendered as a fixed-stretch RGB composite ( R = B12 / SWIR2 ,  G = B11 / SWIR1 ,  B = B8A / NIR ) so flaming combustion is separable from cloud, smoke, fresh char, and bright reflective surfaces. Masks were generated automatically with a  modified HOTMAP SWIR hotspot rule  (confirmed flame where B12 and B12/B8A exceed conservative thresholds, plus a connected growth tier for cooler front margins). Pixel values are  0 = background ,  1 = active fire , and  255 = no-data  (outside the acquisition footprint). The corpus uses a  leak-free fire holdout : whole incidents are assigned to partitions ( 18 train / 3 validation / 4 test ), so evaluation measures transfer to unseen fires rather than random chips from the same landscape. This archive includes: images/  and  masks/  (2,148 PNG files each) summary.csv  (chip-level metadata) partitions.csv  (fire → split assignment) analyst_review/hand_masks/  ( 233  independently reviewed test chips;  54%  of the test split), for quantifying weak-label agreement at chip/cluster level Companion  code , labelling protocol, baseline training scripts, and manuscript figures are available at:   https://github.com/MohammadrezaNarimaniUCDavis/California_Sentinel2_Active_Fire_Dataset This dataset supports a data article prepared for submission to  Data in Brief (Elsevier).

items.summary: Replication data and code for an analysis of how allocation procedures shape which Italian municipalities obtain Recovery and Resilience Facility resources, and whether they convert them into completed works. The package covers 68,990 projects implemented by municipal governments across 36 plan measures, extracted from the OpenPNRR REST API at the ReGiS extraction date of 13 June 2026. Each project carries a coded allocation regime — open window, competitive, administrative assignment, or decentralised regional selection — reconstructed from the administrative activation procedure and, where that field is blank, from the founding decrees of the measures concerned. Contents: the analytical dataset (31 variables); a codebook; a procedure coding table with the normative source of every coding decision; a crosswalk matching 39 measures to the official monitoring of the statutory 40 per cent Southern allocation obligation; municipality-level residuals from the implementation models; global Moran's I under three alternative spatial weight matrices; local Moran statistics on the downstream residual; the reported model results; the extraction script; and a replication script that reproduces the dataset and every estimate from the raw inputs. WHY THIS PACKAGE IS NECESSARY. The primary source is neither versioned nor stable. While this dataset was being constructed, the same endpoint returned 280,767 records dated 26 February 2026 and, hours later, 291,387 records dated 13 June 2026, while the published CSV files carried 298,338 records; between those two responses the numeric identifiers of both projects and implementing organisations were reassigned. A replication attempt that re-downloaded from source would not reproduce these figures, and no version parameter is available to request a specific extraction. The archived snapshot in this package is the only reproducible reference. TWO TRAPS THAT FAIL SILENTLY. ISTAT codes and fiscal codes lose leading zeros if read as numeric, producing empty joins with no error; in the source organisation register, fiscal codes are stored inconsistently with and without leading zeros, and normalising to eleven digits reduces 13,126 records labelled as municipalities to 7,902 distinct entities. Numeric project identifiers are not stable join keys, coinciding across extractions in only 52.9 per cent of cases; the CUP is not unique. Use the local project code. SPATIAL ANALYSIS. Municipal geometries are the official Istat boundaries at 1 January 2021, joined on the six-digit code. The boundary file is not redistributed here and should be obtained from Istat. Three weight matrices are reported — queen contiguity, eight nearest neighbours and a fifty-kilometre distance band — because they are not interchangeable on subsamples: queen contiguity strands as isolates not only islands but mainland municipalities whose neighbours do not belong to the subsample, and those units are dropped silently from the statistic. Isolate counts are reported for every specification. The duration residual was the pre-specified primary diagnostic and the downstream residual was examined subsequently; both are reported in that order. The package contains no personal data: all implementing bodies are public administrations.
items.title: Allocation regimes and the territorial conversion of recovery funds: replication package for 71,548 municipal projects under Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan

items.summary: This repository contains supplementary documentation for a qualitative interview study examining how Bachelor of Software Engineering students understand and use generative AI in their studies. The study investigates: (1) the roles students assign to generative AI and how these roles are enacted; (2) how generative AI transforms learning and software-development tasks and how students legitimize its adoption; and (3) how students negotiate and exercise agency when working with generative AI. The package includes: the interview guide and replication material; First Cycle codebooks organized by research question; Second Cycle Pattern Codes and explanations of their analytical development; a code-saturation monitoring record tracing code emergence, elaboration, and confirmation across interviews; and supplementary evidence tables supporting the reported findings. The interviews were analyzed using the two-cycle coding approach described by Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. First Cycle coding combined descriptive, process, and values-oriented codes. During Second Cycle analysis, conceptually related First Cycle codes were synthesized into broader Pattern Codes. Interview recordings and full transcripts are not publicly available because they contain potentially identifying contextual information and were collected under confidentiality commitments. The package therefore supports analytical transparency and methodological replication without releasing the underlying confidential data. The materials should be interpreted in relation to the educational and institutional context reported in the associated publication. The codebooks and Pattern Codes represent an inductively developed analytical framework rather than a universal taxonomy of student AI adoption.

items.summary: This dataset provides a harmonized global collection of river discharge (Q), suspended sediment concentration (SSC), and suspended sediment load (SSL) observations for source-traceable sediment-data analysis and model evaluation. It integrates observations from multiple monitoring networks, regional datasets, literature compilations, and satellite-derived products, with standardized metadata, coordinates, temporal information, variable definitions, and units. Missing sediment variables are derived where appropriate, gauge locations are linked to MERIT-Basins river reaches and upstream drainage units, and variable-level quality flags are provided to distinguish good, derived, suspect, bad, and missing values. Provenance information is preserved so that released records can be traced to their contributing source stations and datasets. The release consists of three complementary components. The main station-reference component contains 7,135 unique stations and 2,997,121 records from 17 source datasets spanning 1912–2025, distributed as separate daily, monthly, and annual station-by-time NetCDF products according to source-reported temporal support. The climatology auxiliary component contains 1,361 stations from five sources and provides long-term or climatological Q, SSC, and SSL information, with reported source coverage extending from 1884 to 2017. The satellite-derived auxiliary component contains 38,550 locations and 16,478,276 records from three source datasets spanning 1984–2020 and provides complementary spatial coverage, mainly for SSC. The archive includes the daily, monthly, and annual NetCDF products; climatology and satellite-derived auxiliary NetCDF products and their accompanying query catalogues; station, source-station, and source-dataset catalogues; and dataset documentation. The catalogues preserve station-level and source-level provenance and support station screening, source tracing, and reproducible use of the released products. The main station-reference component is intended for station-level time-series extraction, source-traceable benchmarking, and evaluation of hydrological, river-routing, erosion, sediment-transport, and land-surface models. The climatology and satellite-derived components provide complementary long-term and spatial context and should not be treated as direct substitutes for the time-resolved station-reference products. Daily, monthly, and annual products represent different temporal support and should be selected according to the requirements of each analysis rather than combined without accounting for observation coverage. This dataset is intended as a reusable and extensible community resource. Future releases may incorporate additional observations and improvements to the harmonization and integration framework while preserving versioned releases for reproducibility.
items.title: A Harmonized Global Station-Reference Dataset of River Discharge, Suspended Sediment Concentration, and Suspended Sediment Load

items.summary: Automated risk decisions increasingly depend on probabilistic assessments transmitted across organisational and computational boundaries. A probability estimate may remain numerically intact while losing the contextual information required to evaluate its evidentiary dependence — a condition we term Provenance Loss . We introduce Orphaned Inference — a probabilistic output P ( H | E ) that propagates downstream after its contextual qualification is stripped at a transmission boundary — and show that when downstream agents continue scalar-posterior updating using marginal likelihood ratios, the resulting propagation is equivalent to a Na ̈ıve-Bayes-style independence approximation over the correlated evidence sequence. This double-counts the shared environmental signal, producing Directional Context Amplification , quantified by the Cumulative Provenance Amplification (CPA n ) metric. Under environmental context drift ( C 0 → C 1 ), accumulated phantom certainty persists into the post-shift regime as Post-Shift Epistemic Persistence , driving the mean absolute posterior error close to 1 in true-negative states ( H = 0) during the pre-shift period. In risk-analysis terms, provenance loss separates the numerical value of a risk estimate from the evidentiary conditions under which it remains decision-valid: downstream decision makers may receive an apparently precise probability whose effective evidentiary weight is substantially overstated. A Monte Carlo simulation ( N = 5 , 000 trials, n = 15 agent chain) demonstrates the predicted cascade under the specified parameter regime and documents monotone growth of CPA n across sampled correlation values ρ ∈ { 0 , . . . , 0 . 8 } . We propose three provenance-aware risk-control safeguards and discuss their governance trade-offs.
items.title: Orphaned Inferences in Automated Risk Hierarchies: Na ̈ıve Bayes Amplification under Provenance Loss

items.summary: Mathematical problem-solving ability is one of the core competencies students must master, particularly in the topic of Systems of Linear Equations in Two Variables (SLETV), which requires stepwise reasoning and the mathematical modeling of contextual situations. This study aims to examine the effect of implementing the Problem-Based Learning (PBL) model integrated with generative AI technology on students' mathematical problem-solving ability in the SLETV topic. This research employed a quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design. The population consisted of eighth-grade students at a junior high school, with samples selected through purposive sampling and divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group received PBL instruction enriched with generative AI used as a virtual tutor and a generator of contextual problem illustrations, while the control group received conventional PBL instruction without generative AI assistance. Data were collected through a mathematical problem-solving test based on Polya's indicators and analyzed using an independent t-test after normality and homogeneity assumptions were satisfied. The results show that the mean problem-solving score of the experimental group was significantly higher than that of the control group. These findings indicate that integrating generative AI into the PBL syntax strengthens the stages of problem orientation, exploration of solution strategies, and student reflection on the SLETV topic, thereby resulting in a more optimal improvement of mathematical problem-solving ability compared to conventional PBL instruction.
tags: Problem-Based Learning, Generative AI, Mathematical Problem-Solving Ability, SLETV

items.summary: The Earth That Heard is not presented as a literary reconstruction built around biblical verses. It records a textual architecture that the author argues is already present in the Torah itself — a structure that emerged through fifteen years of research into Biblical Hebrew morphology, roots, recurring letter patterns, and the internal organization of the text. The essay traces a continuous thread from the murder of Abel in Genesis to Joshua’s altar on Mount Ebal. Motifs that initially appear independent — earth and blood, firstfruit and firstborn, field and El Shaddai, rising and place, sacrifice, Shechem, the opening of the earth, and the return of the firstfruits — progressively converge into a single narrative structure. The central proposal is that Abel’s unfinished offering, Cain’s failure, and the wounded earth are not abandoned episodes: their resolution unfolds across the Torah and reaches completion in Joshua. The work explicitly separates three epistemic levels: Text — what the biblical text states; Reading — what emerges when distant passages are compared; and Implication — the larger interpretation suggested by the resulting structure. The pattern is also tested quantitatively. The present essay contains 136 key verses; the original connection-density test was performed on a pre-set group of 124 verses selected by the narrative. Using the Control Alphabet / Mandatory Root morphology developed in The Road and the Place , the observed network produced Z = 19.37 (p < 0.0002) against 5,000 random permutations. A second, deliberately simpler test removes the seven control letters א, מ, ת, נ, י, ה, ו from every word and performs direct string matching with no root database; it still yields Z = 10.29 (p < 0.0002) , with the same major long-range connections rising to the top. A raw-word test remains significant at Z = 5.17 (p = 0.0013) . A separate anthology comparison tests whether similarly chosen biblical themes automatically generate the same effect. The Ebal/Shechem axis reaches Z = 17.35 , compared with Covenant Z = 10.07 , Jerusalem/Temple Z = 1.60 , Joseph Z = −8.13 , and Tabernacle Z = −7.16 . The result does not statistically prove the theological interpretation; it shows that the textual concentration being interpreted is itself measurable and unusual. A scientific appendix further examines comparative anatomical and genomic parallels associated with one of the essay’s most unexpected motifs, while explicitly distinguishing scientific observation from midrashic interpretation. After fifteen years of work, the author does not regard this as a story invented to fit the text, but as part of a larger architecture that the text itself gradually disclosed — a structure he considers himself fortunate to have uncovered, even if only in part, and to place on record now. Bilingual publication: Hebrew original and English edition.
items.title: The Earth That Listened — The Hidden Timeline from Genesis to Joshua

items.summary: This deposit contains the results replication package for the article “Governing the Eurasian Roundabout: Anti-Circumvention Governance and Post-Soviet Intermediaries after 2022.” It reconstructs the article’s quantitative trade evidence from archived Eurostat Easy Comext data and provides structured versions of all numbered tables and figures. The product-specific analysis covers monthly EU27 exports from January 2019 through December 2025 for the 50 six-digit Harmonized System codes in the February 2024 Common High Priority Items list and 13 destinations. The workflow constructs the balanced product–partner–month panel, aggregates partner–month exports, calculates raw and normalized summaries, compares product-specific growth with total-export growth, estimates descriptive partner- and month-fixed-effects paths, and reproduces the reported comparison windows and sensitivity checks. The reconstructed evidence shows a sharp contraction in mean monthly EU exports of Common High Priority Items to Russia, from EUR 295.7 million in 2021 to EUR 3.3 million in 2023–2025, alongside increases from EUR 13.934 million to EUR 30.835 million for Kazakhstan and from EUR 1.319 million to EUR 4.496 million for Armenia. Product-specific export growth exceeded total-export growth in both focal destinations, by 14.1 index points in Kazakhstan and 74.2 index points in Armenia. The package also reproduces the pre-event diagnostic, late-2021 contrast, alternative normalizations, product and comparison-set checks, alternative windows, destination distribution, and descriptive policy-milestone summaries. These results are descriptive and corroborative. They do not identify onward shipment, circumvention, ultimate buyers or end users, enforcement effectiveness, or causal policy effects. The archived product-specific and total-export series come from different Eurostat data vintages, and the broad comparison is interpreted accordingly. Run the complete analysis from the extracted package directory with one command: python3 reproduce.py This deposit is associated with the results package at https://zenodo.org/records/19206576 that supports former version of the article.
items.title: Governing the Eurasian Roundabout: Anti-Circumvention Governance and Post-Soviet Intermediaries after 2022. V2

items.summary: Python package and command-line tool that estimates the share of variance in an antimicrobial resistance phenotype carried by the lineages of a bacterial collection, from a lineage label and a susceptibility call or a recorded dilution, and refuses the estimate where the collection cannot support one. One collection admits three quantities and the package reports them apart: the lineage-membership share, what a rule scored out of sample reaches, with a lineage bootstrap; the design-corrected component ratio of the same collection, with an interval exact under the Gaussian one-way model by inversion of a noncentral F; and the superpopulation share for the species, with a chi-square layer on the number of lineages. Each is scored against its own truth on 135 simulated cells from five lineages to a thousand, and each sits behind a gate that refuses where the collection cannot identify the quantity or the residuals contradict the law the interval assumes, the coverage of each having been measured. A binary share is restated on the latent scale of the threshold model beside the observed scale. The lineage label may be a sequence type, a core-genome or SNP cluster, or a serovar, so the same estimate can be read at two typing resolutions. For a difference in non-wild-type prevalence between two collections it applies the Kitagawa decomposition to split the difference into a lineage-composition component and a within-lineage rate component, with a shared-support gate calibrated against measured interval coverage, a test for lineage labels that are differentially and informatively missing, and Benjamini-Yekutieli control within each component family of the antimicrobial panel, valid whatever the dependence between agents. Ships a Streptococcus suis case study (677 isolates, 650 porcine and 27 human, with full data provenance) read at population-cluster and at sequence-type resolution, together with a 720,000-decomposition calibration study and a head-to-head comparison against lineage-adjusted logistic regression. The package reads two tables and never a genome. A susceptibility panel is read at its recorded resolution: a dichotomised call and a recorded dilution are both intervals on the log2 concentration scale and enter one interval likelihood, so the input mode changes how much an observation carries rather than what is estimated. The interval is exact where every reading is a point and calibrated by simulation where a reading is an interval, and the tested wells are taken from the recorded values unless the panel is supplied. Each share carries an e-value; a run that declares the intake each isolate arrived in also carries the running product over intakes, a test supermartingale that may be read after any intake, with the panel decision taken on the log scale so that evidence too strong for a float is still evidence. False-discovery control across the panel holds under arbitrary dependence. The attribution is exercised outside the shipped cohorts on fifty organisms of one NCBI Pathogen Detection release, each taken at the release accession the retrieval recorded: every agent of every cohort that reaches the estimator leaves one record, estimated or refused with the condition that failed, 192 cells are estimated in twelve species and 44 admitted by the support gate in six, and every cell carries a permuted-label control. The Streptococcus suis cohort is read at three definitions of a lineage, population cluster, serotype and sequence type, with the reference label rerun on each other label's own isolates so that the label is separated from the collection. A veterinary arm cuts the same source by host species and by sampling matrix and runs every cell at two definitions of a lineage, the Pathogen Detection SNP cluster and the serovar, with the permuted-label control at both.
